newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures were hit by a wave of selling after stronger than expected German economic data gave traders a pretext to take some profits after the contract hit a high earlier on Wednesday.

Traders said, however, the selloff was measured and it did not signal much of a change in the overall bullish environment for the French bond market. Indeed some said the decline prompted some buying of cash bonds by domestics.
"It was a normal trading day, it was by no means a bloodbath," said a futures trader. "If you think the Ifo is going to keep the market down you've got another thing coming."

The December contract found support at 127.68 after reaching a high of 128.14 early in the session. Traders said selling by a Swiss bank, probably fund driven, had been one of the notable features of the session.
The 10-year spread over Bunds remained steady at minus one basis point.
PIBOR contracts suffered slightly from a weaker franc but stayed close to the contract high of 96.53 reached yesterday, with hopes for French interest rate cuts maintaining the positive mood.
The franc bore the brunt of selling after former French president Giscard d'Estaing urged a depreciation of the franc and a member of the ruling coalition also called for a weaker franc.
The French unit slipped to a low of 3.3847, down from 3.3797 per mark on Tuesday, and was trading at 3.3835 late in the session.
Call money was left unchanged, but economists said a lowering of the overnight rate, was still on the cards.
The early focus on Thursday will be the regular Treasury auction of two- and five-year BTANs. The results of the auction will be released from 1000 GMT.
